staged_source_snapshot.description: This is the exact staged vulnerable source tree whose line map matches the saved AddressSanitizer crash. It also contains the untracked `fuzzing/Fuzz_chpw.c` harness used by Stage 01.

classification.classification_note: The observed memory-safety fault is a 1-byte heap out-of-bounds write in `krb5int_utf8_normalize()`. Source-level root cause is that the `KRB5_UTF8_APPROX` branch compatibility-decomposes attacker-controlled Unicode into more ASCII bytes than the original UTF-8 length but never performs the capacity check and `realloc()` that exist on the non-approx path.

bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced the crash against the staged krb5 checkout `d864d740d019fdf2c640460f2aa2760c7fa4d5e9`, an ancestor of both metadata commits, using the untracked harness `fuzzing/Fuzz_chpw.c`. The exact staged `poc` is 20 bytes: `20 20 20 20 e3 8e af e3 8e af 20 20 e3 8e af 20 20 e3 8e af`, which is four spaces, U+33AF, U+33AF, two spaces, U+33AF, two spaces, and U+33AF. `krb5_chpw_message()` first calls `decode_ad_policy_info(server_string, &msg)`, but `decode_ad_policy_info()` rejects the witness immediately because `data->length` is 20 instead of `AD_POLICY_INFO_LENGTH` 30. Control then reaches the NUL-free UTF-8 branch at lines 494-496, which calls `krb5int_utf8_normalize(server_string, &string, KRB5_UTF8_APPROX)`. Inside `krb5int_utf8_normalize()`, the mixed ASCII/non-ASCII path allocates `outsize = len + 7 = 27` bytes from the original UTF-8 length. Because the first non-ASCII byte is `s[4]`, lines 174-175 copy only the first three leading spaces into `out` and leave `outpos == 3`, while lines 193-195 carry the fourth leading space into the first `ucs` block. The UTF-8 decode loop turns each `e3 8e af` sequence into U+33AF, and `uccompatdecomp()` then uses the staged compatibility-table entry `_uckdcmp_nodes` `0x000033af -> 0x000010b0`, whose `_uckdcmp_decomp` sequence at that offset is `0072 0061 0064 2215 0073 0032`. Each U+33AF therefore contributes five copied ASCII bytes after the non-ASCII division slash U+2215 is filtered out by `ucsout[j] < 0x80`. The first `[space, U+33AF, U+33AF]` block moves `outpos` to 14. The next separator writes one space directly to `out` and carries one into the middle `[space, U+33AF]` block, whose own approx-copy loop moves `outpos` from 15 to 21. The second separator again writes one space and carries one, so `outpos` reaches 22 before the final `[space, U+33AF]` block. The same unguarded approx loop then attempts six more ASCII writes (`space`, `r`, `a`, `d`, `s`, `2`); the final `2` lands at index 27, overrunning the 27-byte heap allocation at `ucstr.c:238`. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at `krb5int_utf8_normalize`, with the destination buffer allocated at `ucstr.c:169`. The patch removes this vulnerable normalization call from `krb5_chpw_message()` and replaces it with UTF-8 validation plus `k5memdup0()`, avoiding the under-sized approximate-normalization buffer entirely.

evidence_limitations: The staged reproducing tree is checkout `d864d740d019fdf2c640460f2aa2760c7fa4d5e9` plus the untracked harness `fuzzing/Fuzz_chpw.c`, not a clean checkout of metadata commit `f368c75dd867965cd621d011a6770e940af4047d`. The staged commit is an ancestor of both metadata commits and matches the saved ASan line map.

Stage 01 reproduced only the vulnerable AddressSanitizer crash. The fixed path was not executed in this Stage 02 session, so `patch_resolves` remains false as a runtime-evidence field even though the patch removes the vulnerable normalization call.

Runtime disambiguation was disabled in `run_flags.json`, so no extra instrumentation was permitted. The exact overflowing byte and block lengths are therefore derived statically from the saved PoC bytes plus the in-tree Unicode decomposition tables.

fine_trace.note: The harness accepts sizes 20 through 100. The saved 20-byte witness passes that check and is wrapped as `DataInput` for `krb5_chpw_message()` without modification.
This call is the first project-side consumption of the fuzzer buffer. It sends the same 20-byte `server_string` into the AD-policy parser attempt before any UTF-8 handling.
`data->length` is 20, so this gate rejects the AD-policy interpretation because `AD_POLICY_INFO_LENGTH` is 30. The function returns 0 with `*msg_out` still NULL.

After the parser attempt leaves `msg == NULL`, the same buffer still satisfies `length > 0` and `memchr(..., 0, 20) == NULL`, so `krb5_chpw_message()` calls `krb5int_utf8_normalize()` with `KRB5_UTF8_APPROX`.
The normalizer aliases the attacker-controlled bytes as `s` and copies the byte length into `len`; on the witness, `len == 20`.
On the mixed ASCII/non-ASCII path with `casefold` clear, the destination buffer is sized from the original UTF-8 byte length only. `len + 7` yields a 27-byte heap allocation.
The initial ASCII scan stops before `s[4]`, the first non-ASCII byte. The function copies only `s[0..2]` into `out`, leaving `outpos == 3`.
The preceding ASCII character `s[3]` is not in `out`; it is carried into `ucs[0]`, so the first non-ASCII block begins with a space already queued for decomposition.
The UTF-8 decode loop consumes `e3 8e af` twice and appends `U+33AF` twice after the carried space, so `ucs[0..2]` becomes `[0x20, U+33AF, U+33AF]`.
`uccompatdecomp()` expands that first block to 13 code points: the carried space plus two copies of `r a d U+2215 s 2`.

fine_trace.var: approx, out, outpos, outsize, ucsout, ucsoutlen
fine_trace.note: Unlike the non-approx sibling at lines 249-257, this loop has no `outsize - outpos` guard. From the 13-code-point first block it copies 11 bytes (space plus `rads2` twice), advancing `outpos` from 3 to 14.

The raw-byte growth check just above this loop sees `len - i == 10` and `outsize - outpos == 13`, so `out` stays 27 bytes. This separator loop then writes `s[10]` to `out` (`outpos` 14 -> 15) and carries `s[11]` into `*ucs` for the next block.
The next non-ASCII run decodes `e3 8e af` once after the carried space, so `ucs[0..1]` becomes `[0x20, U+33AF]`.
`uccompatdecomp()` expands `[0x20, U+33AF]` to seven code points: space plus `r a d U+2215 s 2`.
The same unguarded approx loop copies the six ASCII entries from the middle block, moving `outpos` from 15 to 21.

The raw-byte growth check again stays false because `len - i == 5` and `outsize - outpos == 6`, so `out` is still 27 bytes. This separator loop writes `s[15]` to `out` (`outpos` 21 -> 22) and carries `s[16]` into `*ucs` for the final block.
The last non-ASCII run decodes the final `e3 8e af` after the carried space, so `ucs[0..1]` again becomes `[0x20, U+33AF]`.
The final `uccompatdecomp()` call again produces seven code points, space plus `r a d U+2215 s 2`. At this point `outpos == 22`, so only indices 22 through 26 remain inside the 27-byte allocation.

The final approx-copy loop writes the carried space at index 22, `r`/`a`/`d`/`s` at 23-26, skips U+2215, and then attempts `'2'` at index 27. AddressSanitizer reports that one-byte write immediately to the right of the region allocated at line 169.

allocation_context.note: AddressSanitizer attributes the overflowed 27-byte region to this `malloc(outsize)` call. On the witnessed path `outsize` came from `len + 7` with `len == 20`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The ASan allocation frame identifies the 27-byte destination buffer from fine-trace step 5. The root cause is the missing capacity check on the approx branch in step 10, which lets that fixed-size allocation remain in place while decomposition expands the witness beyond it.
